summary: Vinhos is a dense Vital Lacerda economic game where players run rival Portuguese wineries, buying vineyards, hiring oenologists, producing and aging wine, then selling it through trade fairs, exports, and critics' ratings. It's a heavy, fiddly euro with lots of interlocking subsystems and a fair amount of bookkeeping, rewarded by a satisfying sense of running a real business.
praised: gorgeous Ian O'Toole art and production in the Deluxe Edition
meaningful long-term planning and multiple viable strategies
criticised: steep rules overhead and long teach
wine-quality dice rolls introduce noticeable luck
long playtime that can drag with new players

interaction.kind: competing for regional area majority and market/order-track position, with catch-the-leader hindrances
interaction.detail: Players vie for majority control in shared wine regions and for position on the wine-order/demand track, and a catch-the-leader mechanism actively hampers whoever is ahead. Even so, a large share of each turn goes into building and upgrading your own private vineyard and winery engine.

scoring.how_you_win: Across 6 years, choose action-wheel spaces to plant vines, build wineries, produce and age wine, and sell it at fairs or export it; the player with the most combined VP from wine quality sold, vineyards, buildings, and leftover money at the end wins.
